top_entities.name: India
top_entities.news_summary: The UN Human Rights Office said on 2026-10-10 it was concerned by mass detentions of demonstrators, protest leaders, civil-society members, lawyers and journalists around Delhi protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which demand the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation over electoral-roll revision; it urged immediate and unconditional release of those arbitrarily detained and dialogue with protesters. India's Ministry of External Affairs rejected the statement as unwarranted interference. Press counts of those detained range from 700+ at Jantar Mantar to about 1,000 across Delhi (unverified figures).
top_entities.reason: UN Human Rights Office public concern over mass detentions of protesters, lawyers and journalists in Delhi; government rejected the statement. Major negative civil-liberties event within the last 7 days.

top_entities.name: Lisbon
top_entities.news_summary: Thousands protested in Lisbon and Porto on 2026-10-11 over rising living costs and housing prices (platform 'Nao da mais para viver assim', with actions also in Aveiro, Braga and Funchal), per Euronews. The Portugal Post separately reports a parliament vigil against government plans to speed evictions and remove the annual rent-increase cap ahead of a 30 September debate (undated URL; unverified).
top_entities.reason: Nationwide housing/cost-of-living protests (2026-10-11) with Lisbon the main venue, amid government plans to speed evictions and lift the rent-increase cap; municipal housing-response signal for a stale, near-band-boundary city.

A prison-technicians' pay/housing-cost strike in Porto on 2026-10-06 is reported by The Portugal Post (undated URL).
top_entities.reason: Housing protest march (2026-10-11) followed by a police-cleared protest camp (RTP, 2026-10-12); city-level policing/housing signal.

The UN Human Rights Office statement of 2026-10-10 urged release of those arbitrarily detained, including lawyers and journalists.

top_entities.name: Texas
top_entities.news_summary: Texas executed Jamaal Howard, 46, by single-dose pentobarbital lethal injection at Huntsville on 2026-10-07 (seventh Texas execution of 2026; reported as the 30th US execution this year), one week after Tennessee's failed Christa Pike execution. His lawyers cited the Pike failure and unresolved questions about the safety of Texas's compounded pentobarbital supply and sought a 30-day delay; Gov. Abbott did not respond and the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals and U.S. Supreme Court rejected late filings.
top_entities.reason: Texas executed Jamaal Howard by pentobarbital a week after Tennessee's failed execution, over unresolved drug-supply safety objections; stale entity in a state-execution pattern.

top_entities.name: Sudan
top_entities.news_summary: The World Food Programme condemned an aerial strike in the early hours of 2026-10-03 on two clearly marked WFP-contracted trucks travelling from Dilling to Kadugli in South Kordofan, killing one driver; a day earlier a WFP truck hit an explosive device in Dilling after delivering food. WFP called for a prompt, impartial investigation. Sudan Tribune also reports a UN humanitarian-chief condemnation (not independently confirmed).
top_entities.reason: Aerial strike killed a driver on marked WFP-contracted aid trucks in South Kordofan (2026-10-03) a day after another WFP truck hit an explosive device; humanitarian-access violation in a famine-affected conflict.

top_entities.name: United States
top_entities.news_summary: Human Rights Watch reported on 2026-10-02 that ICE detained Mark Mabasa, son of slain Philippine journalist Percival 'Percy Lapid' Mabasa, on 2026-09-21 and holds him at the Adelanto ICE processing center in California despite a pending asylum claim and earlier death threats, citing the UN Human Rights Committee position that detaining asylum seekers without individualized justification is arbitrary.
top_entities.reason: HRW report that ICE is detaining the asylum-seeking son of a slain Philippine journalist despite prior death threats; immigration-detention civil-rights signal (federal level).

top_entities.name: Russia
top_entities.news_summary: An explosion and fire hit the Rostec-owned Krasnozavodsk chemical plant in the Moscow region on 2026-10-01. Early reports citing the Shot channel said seven were killed and 40+ evacuated; later reporting citing emergency services via TASS said one person died, five were missing and 44 were in the building. The cause (technical failure vs attack) is unconfirmed and the toll is unsettled.
top_entities.reason: Fatal explosion/fire at a Rostec chemical plant (2026-10-01); death toll disputed (7 per Shot vs 1 confirmed per TASS); industrial-safety and transparency signal. Cause unconfirmed.

top_entities.name: Cornell University
top_entities.news_summary: On 2026-10-01 New York Gov. Kathy Hochul signed an executive order naming Attorney General Letitia James special prosecutor in the case of an alleged 2024 gang rape of a Cornell student (Reuters, republished 2026-10-02), citing loss of faith in the Tompkins County DA after no one was charged. A civil suit filed 2026-09-16 names Cornell, seven Chi Phi members, the fraternity, a bar and the plaintiff's sorority. Cornell says it ran a comprehensive investigation and barred the Chi Phi chapter. The allegations are unproven.
top_entities.reason: NY governor removed the Tompkins County DA from an alleged 2024 campus gang-rape case and named the state AG special prosecutor (2026-10-01); institutional-response and Title IX-type handling signal; allegations unproven.

top_entities.name: Tennessee
top_entities.news_summary: Tennessee's attempt to execute Christa Pike by pentobarbital lethal injection on 2026-09-30 failed after two doses; she was hospitalized in critical condition. On 2026-10-01 Gov. Bill Lee halted all remaining 2026 executions, ordered an independent third-party review (former U.S. Attorney Ed Stanton retained) and accepted the resignation of Corrections Commissioner Frank Strada. Tennessee Lookout (2026-10-02) calls it the state's second botched execution this year, after Tony Carruthers in May; legislators of both parties are seeking oversight or reform.
top_entities.reason: Failed execution of Christa Pike (2026-09-30), state halt of all 2026 executions and independent review (2026-10-01); second botched execution in 2026. Major negative state-justice event.

degraded_scan_quality.summary: The search backend handles long OR-chains poorly: for most T2 batch queries the returned results referenced only a few of the 10-12 named entities, and generic/undated pages dominate. Absence of results for an entity inside a batch therefore means 'not surfaced', not 'confirmed clean'. T1 individual searches had the same recency weakness (many returned archive pages).
degraded_scan_quality.tool_error_note: invalid_tool_input errors were returned by the search tool for queries containing a slash inside a quoted name (e.g. Cullen/Frost, Anthem/Elevance) and for some long quoted lists; in each error case a generic fallback search ran, so those first attempts are not counted as batch coverage.
degraded_scan_quality.api_errors_not_counted: Two domain-restricted verification calls (allowed_domains included apnews.com/reuters.com/tennessean.com) returned HTTP 400 before running and are not counted as searches.
degraded_scan_quality.sector_queries_with_no_in_window_results: Most T3 sweeps returned no in-window dated items; in-window evidence was found through T2 batches (Delhi, Texas) and date-targeted T3 sweeps (UN OHCHR, HRW).

search_accounting.tier_1_combined_precursor_note: Early in the run seven T1 queries combined 2-5 T1 entities (Rex/Sanchez; Enservco/Erie; Gran Tierra/Halcon/Hercules; Recursion/Tempus; Watts/Xcel; Dongguan/Fuzhou/Harbin/Jinan/Kunming; Lisbon/Porto). They did not satisfy the one-search-per-entity rule, so each of those 18 entities was re-searched individually; the 7 precursor queries are counted in searches_performed but not in tier_1_individual_searches.
search_accounting.tier_2_retry_note: 13 extra T2 calls were retries of batches whose first query returned a tool error (batch 14 needed two retries).

stats.window_note: Evidence dates must be >= 2026-10-01 under validate-scan.mjs window arithmetic (windowEnd 2026-10-14T23:59:59Z minus 14 days); Tennessee is therefore dated 2026-10-01 (governor's halt and review) although the failed execution itself was 2026-09-30.
stats.date_conventions: evidence_date is the date of the underlying event or statement where a source states it; some sources are republished one to two days later (validator WARNs on those cases are expected: Sudan, Cornell, Tennessee).
stats.tiering_note: T1 = top 150 by base_priority (staleness + importance + volatility + pending-proposal per spec; Universities weighted 5; ties broken alphabetically by slug; pending-proposal flag = status beginning 'pending' in research/change-proposals/; no sector systemic-transition bonus). Evidence-found entities are scored news_score + base_priority (capped at 100). Entities flagged via T2/T3 retain tier T2.
stats.batch_size_note: 101 sector-coherent batches of 10-12 entities (per-index, ordered by sector/region).
stats.batch_query_note: batch_query is the query as issued; entity names were lightly normalised (diacritics, legal suffixes, quotes/slashes) relative to the roster for some batches.
stats.top_entities_note: Eleven flagged targets, below the 20-30 requested: only items with a verifiable in-window source date were promoted. Many stronger-looking stories were dropped as out-of-window, undated-only, or misdated (see dropped_candidates). Padding was deliberately avoided per validate-scan.mjs section 6.
stats.overage_explanation: T2 used 114 calls for 101 batches (13 retries after tool errors), T3 used 25 sweeps (10 above the 15 floor, within the 15-25 band), 16 verification searches were run (6 above the allowance, because several candidates needed first-pass and second-pass date corroboration), and 7 combined T1 precursor queries were run before being redone individually.
